chunks: And Hisham ibn Salim narrated from Abu Basir, who said:
I heard Abu Abdullah عليه السلام say: “Whoever is offered the opportunity to perform hajj, even if on a maimed donkey with a cut-off tail, and he refuses, then he is considered capable of hajj.”

key_terms.أَجْدَعَ: maimed or mutilated, describing the poor condition of the animal
key_terms.الْحَجُّ: hajj, the pilgrimage to the Sacred House that becomes obligatory upon one who is able
key_terms.حِمَارٍ: a donkey, mentioned here as a modest means of transport
key_terms.فَأَبَى: then he refused, meaning he declined despite the availability of means
key_terms.مَقْطُوعِ الذَّنَبِ: with a cut-off tail, further emphasizing hardship and lack of comfort
key_terms.مُسْتَطِيعٌ: deemed capable or able, in the legal sense relevant to the obligation of hajj

ai.seo_question: When is a person considered capable of performing hajj in Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith states that when a person is presented with a viable means to undertake hajj, even under difficult and humble travel conditions, he is regarded as having the required ability. It indicates that legal capacity for hajj is not restricted to comfort or prestige, but is established by the actual possibility of reaching the pilgrimage.
